papers.title: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Overtaking with Bezier Curve Path
papers.abstract: Rapid advancements in autonomous vehicle technology have significantly improved driving safety, yet formulating safe and efficient overtaking strategies remains a key challenge. This study proposes an algorithmic framework for autonomous vehicles to perform overtaking maneuvers, validated through comprehensive simulations. The framework utilizes Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) to manage complex vehicle dynamics, processing real-time velocity and steering angle inputs. Real-time feedback from LiDAR sensors enables dynamic trajectory generation using Bezier curve formulations, which provide reference inputs for the pure pursuit algorithm to guide the NMPC during overtaking. Once the vehicle aligns with the obstacle, the Bezier curve is adjusted to smoothly return the vehicle to its original path. The approach was thoroughly evaluated using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and Gazebo, ensuring realistic visualization and robust performance under dynamic conditions.
papers.venue: JAREE (Journal on Advanced Research in Electrical Engineering)

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究自动驾驶超车的NMPC控制，与用户关注的工程仿真代理模型、FEA或植入物生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses autonomous vehicle trajectory control with NMPC and Bezier curves in ROS/Gazebo, with no surrogate modeling, no FEA/FEM data, no physics-based design optimization, and no biomechanics or implant context.

summary_en.motivation: Safe and efficient overtaking remains a challenging problem in autonomous driving.
summary_en.method: A nonlinear model predictive control framework generates Bezier-curve reference trajectories tracked by a pure pursuit controller using LiDAR feedback.
summary_en.result: The vehicle performs smooth overtaking and path return under simulated dynamic conditions.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated through ROS and Gazebo simulation scenarios.
